title: api-config-runtime-draft-samir-patel.json
content:
Personal scratchpad: API + runtime config shapes for routing/batching/kv-cache. Rough notes - not final.

Goal: define a compact, user-facing config schema that maps to runtime primitives (routing policy, cache config, batching hints, quantization profile, fallbacks). Keep shape small for first pass, then expand with advanced fields behind flags.

1) High-level shape (informal)
- route_id: string (user-visible)
- model: model-id or model-family alias (e.g., redwood/titan-7b, or titan-family/latest)
- version: optional pin or semver range
- routing: {policy, priority, region_preferences}   <-- map to routing layer
- batching: {enabled, target_latency_ms, max_batch_tokens, max_batch_size, batching_strategy}  <-- hints to autoscaler/runner
- cache: {type, enabled, prefix_ttl_ms, kv_mode}  <-- prefix/KV caching config
- quantization_profile: string or object (profile id)
- fallbacks: [ordered list of compatible model ids]
- observability: {trace_sample_rate, sampling_rules}
- limits: {concurrency, qps, token_limit}

Notes: the above has nested fields - for user YAML/JSON it's fine, but our Drive JSONs must be flat. In runtime mapping, flatten into key prefixes for the control plane (e.g., batching.enabled, caching.prefix_ttl_ms).

2) Example user-facing YAML (sketch)
route_id: chat-short-context
model: redwood/titan-7b-v2
version: 2026-01-18
routing:
  policy: latency-first
  region_preferences:
    - us-west1
    - eu-west1
batching:
  enabled: true
  target_latency_ms: 60
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 32
  batching_strategy: continuous
cache:
  enabled: true
  type: prefix
  prefix_ttl_ms: 300000  # 5m
  kv_mode: read-through
quantization_profile: default-8bit
fallbacks:
  - redwood/titan-3b-quant
  - redwood/titan-7b-cpu
observability:
  trace_sample_rate: 0.01
limits:
  concurrency: 8
  qps: 200
  token_limit: 8192

Questions / open items:
- Naming conventions for profiles: do we require org-scoped names (org/profile) or global registry?
- How to express "soft" vs "hard" constraints (target_latency_ms is soft; concurrency is hard) - need explicit field enforcement_policy: soft|hard.
- Back-compat strategy: add a runtime migration plan for old route configs when we introduce new batching controls.
- Validation surface: some fields depend on model (e.g., token_limit depends on model max context) - validate at enrollment time.

Runtime mapping notes (sketch):
- routing.policy -> router::policy (latency-first, cost-first, capacity-aware)
- routing.region_preferences -> router::preferred_regions list; router will fallback to any-region if none available
- batching.* -> batch_manager hints; important: target_latency_ms maps to dynamic windowing heuristic
- cache.type = prefix | full-response; prefix -> enabled kv cache with prefix length heuristic at runtime
- kv_mode = read-through | write-through | read-only (we may start with read-through only)

Edge cases to handle:
- User sets batching.max_batch_size high but model memory prohibits it -> reject at validation with recommended value
- Cache prefix TTL longer than model version lifetime -> warn on deploy, require pinning version or shorter TTL
- Fallbacks include models with different tokenizer behavior -> need compatibility checker (tokenizer/version mismatch)

Operational TODOs (short):
- [ ] Define enforcement_policy enum and wire through validation (owner: Jamie)
- [ ] Add compatibility checker library for tokenizer/arch matches (owner: Casey)
- [ ] Draft API validation errors/messages for typical misconfigs (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Backfill spec doc to Confluence + link in console UI (owner: Product/Console)

Sketch diagram (text):
User config YAML -> Control plane API -> Config validator -> Router config store -> Serving runtime
                                                     -> compatibility checker
                                                     -> batching manager (hints)
                                                     -> kv-cache service (prefix keys)

Small UX notes (for console):
- Show derived runtime hints on the route preview (e.g., projected p50 latency, projected cost per 1k tokens)
- Provide "suggested batching" button that runs sample workload in a sandbox to propose values

Snippets: simple flattened key representation we could accept via API (for easier patching)
route_id: chat-short-context
model: redwood/titan-7b-v2
batching.enabled: true
batching.target_latency_ms: 60
batching.max_batch_size: 32
cache.enabled: true
cache.type: prefix
cache.prefix_ttl_ms: 300000
quantization_profile: default-8bit

Backwards compatibility idea: accept both nested and flattened keys server-side, normalize to canonical nested shape for storage. This makes CLI/patch operations easier.

Last thoughts: keep the first public schema small and conservative. Goal: unblock dedicated/private customers who want predictable latency and caching. Advanced knobs (e.g., dynamic batching_strategy plug-ins) can come later behind feature flags.

Links that matter: Confluence draft (linked above), INF-4123 for compatibility checker, runtime PR 987 for batching manager prototype.

End of scratchpad.
